dedupe_keys.name: stochastic power flow convergence under colored noise matlab implementation

description: The stochastic power-flow authors publish a MATLAB implementation comparing Gauss-Seidel and Newton-Raphson convergence on IEEE 30- and 57-bus systems. Zenodo provides the archive under MIT. The own page describes white-noise and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck perturbations, tracked convergence trajectories, sixty repeated runs with confidence intervals, one thousand Monte Carlo realisations, Taylor-series probabilistic propagation and parameter sensitivity tests. This model can test how stochastic injections affect solver convergence before grid-reliability simulations use either method. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this implementation. Coverage is two benchmark networks and the stated noise processes, not arbitrary national transmission systems. A limitation is that convergence under synthetic coloured noise is not evidence of accuracy under actual renewable forecast errors or protection actions. Monte Carlo and Taylor approximations can diverge outside their assumptions. The archive was not downloaded, MATLAB was not run and confidence intervals were not recalculated.
